text.p: - French court on Tuesday ordered nine French banks to block deposits of the central bank of former Yugoslavia but did not order publishing data about those deposits as Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina have demanded.
- A man suspected of planting a bomb in front of a judge's house on September 24 admitted he was quilty.
- European commissioner Hans van den Broek will visit Slovenia on Thursday when he will meet Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and other high officials.
- Parliament said the cost of the election campaign for each party should not exceed 60 tolars ($0.44) per voter.
- Slovenian Social-Economic Council on Tuesday debated urging employers to cut work benefits, claiming that the high labour costs are hampering Slovenia's competitiveness.
- "Slovenian jurisdiction is too ocuppied with itself and too little occupied with matters important to people," Minister of Jurisdiction Meta Zupancic said on Tuesday.
- Slovenian Office for Macroeconomic Analyses said it doubted Slovenia's GDP growth will reach the forecast 3.3 percent by the end of the year.
